title: A Teaspoon of This Star Weighs a Billion Tons ⭐ #shorts
description:
Neutron stars are the collapsed cores left behind when giant stars explode as supernovas. A typical one packs about 1.4 times the mass of our Sun into a ball only about 20 km (12 miles) across – so a single teaspoon of it would weigh around a billion tons. They were predicted in 1934 and first found in 1967, and the fastest known one spins 716 times every second.

Sources: NASA, Live Science, Science News, Astronomy Magazine, McGill University, Physics World, Smithsonian Magazine

scenes.text: It's a neutron star. What's left after a giant star collapses and explodes as a supernova.
A typical one has about one point four times the mass of our Sun.
But it's squeezed into a ball only about twenty kilometers across. That's the size of a city!
So just one teaspoon of it would weigh around a billion tons.
scenes.label: TONS IN ONE TEASPOON

scenes.text: Scientists predicted these stars in nineteen thirty-four. But nobody found one until nineteen sixty-seven.
And some spin like crazy. The fastest known one turns seven hundred sixteen times every second.
scenes.label: SPINS PER SECOND

scenes.text: A city-sized ball, heavier than our Sun, spinning hundreds of times a second. Space is wild.
